title: A paragraph of inline pictures only is the tallest picture's extent whether it holds one, two or three pictures; a text run beside them adds its descent; a line multiple adds (m - 1) x the mark's single line
source: probe build.py -> Word for Mac direct PDF (2026-10-29), pymupdf control baselines (pitch 73.44 = 60 + 13.44) and image bboxes, Letter, Calibri 11 docDefaults after 0 line 240: one, two, three 60 pt pictures and a 60 + 40 pt pair all make a 60.00 pt paragraph; two pictures + text and one picture + text 62.88 (60 + Calibri descent); two pictures at line 276 62.16, one picture 61.92 (60 + 0.15 x 13.44); effectExtent b = 8 pt on both pictures 67.92; after 160 line 259 two pictures 69.12 = 60 + 8 + 1.12. gen before the fix: 62.68 for every multi-picture row (the inline-block picture wrapper's baseline is its bottom edge, so the trailing break's descent hung under the row)

cases.note: two inline pictures: the picture-only line box, no strut or descent (Word 60.00)
three inline pictures in one row (Word 60.00)
two pictures + a text run: the text descent joins the line (Word 62.88)
line 276: the multiple's extra is the .doc-p-pic padding, not a line-height (Word 62.16)
the editable picture wrapper sits on the line bottom like the picture itself; baseline alignment hung the trailing break's 3.5px descent under every row of two or more pictures
